reading.title: How Living Things Move
reading.purpose: See how animals and people move, and why the right motion word paints a clear picture.
paras: Living things move in many ways, and English has many words for walking and running. Choosing the right word helps readers picture the motion.

Some movements are fast. A cheetah can sprint, running as fast as it can for a short distance. A squirrel will scamper up a tree with quick, light steps. A house cat may sneak toward a toy, moving so quietly that nobody notices.

Other movements are slow. Cows wander across a field with no clear place to go. A family on a sunny afternoon might stroll through a park with no hurry at all. A tired hiker will trudge up a long hill with slow, heavy steps.

Some movements show feelings or trouble. A child who is angry may stomp across the floor with loud steps. A dog with a sore paw will limp, walking unevenly to protect its leg. Within hours of birth, a young horse called a foal can stand. Its first steps stagger, as if it might fall, and its body may lurch forward in a jerky way.
Each word gives a different picture, so pick the one that matches the motion.

qs.q: In paragraph 4, a dog that will "limp" is a dog that
choices: walks unevenly because a paw is sore
walks slowly with no clear place to go
runs fast for a short distance
moves quietly so that nobody notices
qs.why: The sentence explains it: the dog is "walking unevenly to protect its leg."

qs.q: Which sentence tells how a squirrel moves up a tree?
choices: A cheetah can sprint, running as fast as it can for a short distance.
A house cat may sneak toward a toy, moving so quietly that nobody notices.
A squirrel will scamper up a tree with quick, light steps.
qs.why: Only this sentence is about a squirrel, and it says the squirrel moves with quick, light steps.

ev.text: A squirrel will scamper up a tree with quick, light steps.

qs.q: Why do a foal's first steps stagger and lurch?
choices: It is tired from carrying a heavy load up a long, steep hill.
It is angry about something and wants to stomp across the floor.
It has a sore paw and is trying to protect its hurt leg.
It just learned to stand, so walking is new.
qs.why: The reading says these are the foal's first steps, so it makes sense that they are unsteady.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Fast movements are always better than slow movements in every story.
Different words show different movements, so pick the best one.
Only animals can sprint, scamper, or sneak from one place to another.
A hurt animal should never be allowed to walk anywhere on its own.
qs.why: The reading groups words by fast, slow, and troubled movement, and ends by saying to pick the word that matches the motion.

clues.text: running as fast as it can for a short distance
walking unevenly to protect its leg

reading.retellFrame: Writers choose a movement word such as ___ to show ___.

needsReview.reason: Says a foal can stand within hours of birth. This is accurate for horses (foals stand within about an hour), but a person should confirm the wording.
